subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T15:10:00Z
Subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciate the candid conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria you called out, and proposed next steps so we can align internally. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Inference unit economics are currently the top blocker: your avg cost/token on the current endpoint is ~3x what you expected once you scale.
- Latency spikes during peak trading hours cause throttling in downstream pipelines.
- Limited ops capacity to run extensive quantization/benchmark experiments in-house.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Model: finbot/gpt-fin-13b (hosted on AWS)
- Serving: ECS Fargate instances with a custom batching gateway
- Observability: Datadog + custom cost metrics; limited per-request token breakdown

Success criteria you shared:
- Reduce inference unit cost by >=40% without degrading accuracy on reconciliation tasks.
- Maintain 95th pct latency under 350ms for 1k qps bursts during peak windows.
- Minimal engineering lift for initial POC (1-2 week integration window).

What we can help with (high level):
- Quantization + model variant suggestions (FP16, 4-bit options) and expected perf/cost delta for your model family.
- Smart batching and KV cache recommendations tuned to your request distribution (we saw short prompts with high reuse).
- A short cost-modeling exercise to estimate per-call unit economics under different deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood to run a quick cost/latency estimate and share a one-page delta (attached: redwood_estimate_v1.pdf). I included an initial spreadsheet for your team to validate assumptions.
2) Schedule a 45-min technical sync with Rishi (SE) this week to agree on benchmarking plan and sample traces.
3) Procurement and security to get SOC2 evidence (attached SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf).

Would you be available for the SE sync on Thursday 11/30 at 10am PT? If not, propose two alternatives.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood_estimate_v1.pdf; inference-cost-modeling.xlsx; SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finbot.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T16:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and accurate. A few clarifications:
- The 3x number is what we see across requests today after tokenization inefficiencies; on shorter prompts the delta is worse.
- The 95th pct latency target is the customer-facing service SLA; internal processing can be higher but we'd like to keep end-to-end under 500ms.

We can do Thu 11/30 10am PT for the SE sync — Alex (me) + two engineers will join. Procurement looped in for the SOC2.

A couple asks for the estimate:
- Please include assumptions for prompt length distribution and hit-rate for prefix caching.
- If you can show one hosted vs dedicated price comparison for 1M monthly requests, that would help procurement.

I'll confirm attendees tomorrow. Looking forward to the benchmarking plan.

—Alex
Director of Engineering | FinBot
alex.kim@finbot.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T17:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Internal — looping you both in so we can move on the two asks Alex called out:
- Ben: procurement will want a hosted vs dedicated 1M-reqs comparison and a pricing framing we can use in the first email to Procurement. Can you draft a short table + recommended discount cadence for a 12-month commit?
- Rishi: can you lead the SE sync and propose a benchmarking plan (sample traces, quantization matrix, expected delta table for FP16/4-bit + estimated 95th latency) — aim for a 30-45 minute runbook we can execute in the POC window.

I attached the initial model of assumptions (inference-cost-modeling.xlsx). Let's aim to have the draft pricing + SE runbook by EOD Wednesday so I can share w/ Alex before the call.

Thanks — M

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T18:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Ack — I'll prepare a benchmarking plan and an initial quantization matrix. High-level notes I'll include:
- Quick wins: FP16 + 8-bit asymmetric kernels for your model family may give ~25-35% cost reduction with minimal accuracy loss.
- Aggressive option: 4-bit (GPTQ-style) could hit 45-60% reduction but requires validation on recon accuracy.
- Batching: we need to capture your request timestamp distribution; if 30-40% of requests are short and bursty, adaptive batching + prefix caching should cut token compute by ~20-30%.

I'll put a runbook in the Drive link and share before EOD Wed.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
